properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-05-01 to Msl Oil & Gas Corp in Hamilton Twp, McKean county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Msl Oil & Gas Corp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-05-01
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 883847
Permit API: 083-47035
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-05-01
Comments: Brian Ayers of DEP was contacted by MSL's Dick Pascarella on 4/23/2020 regarding a condensate leak from a tank that was found that day. PA Fish and Boat Commission officer Tom Mcmann was on site 4/24/2020 to follow up and took some photos that are included in this report. It appears as though a small, uncontained drip gas tank had a failure at a fitting at some point prior to the spill being found. This tank holds mostly water that condenses from the gas coming from the compressor station nearby, but also contains some condensed petroleum liquids. An estimated 5-10 gallons of this fluid escaped from the broken fitting and was spilled to the ground. Some of this ran down slope toward an UNT of Chappel Fork, with some collecting in a low, wet area and a small amount eventually entering the water. Tom Mcmann documented photos of the condensate in the vernal pool area, which is included in the attached photos. A Department site visit was performed 5/1/2020. The operator has scraped up the surface of the contaminated site, and placed down straw mulch and seed. They also put down gravel around equipment close to the stream and have built containment around the drip gas tank. The area close to the stream was observed to have a strong condensate odor and some sheen could be spotted entering the stream when this area was agitated on the stream banks. Some product was noted, mostly in the form of sheen, in the UNT Chappel Fork. The stream crosses Chappel Fork Rd a few feet from where the product entered, and sheen was visible upon agitation approximately 150-200 feet downstream. No free product was apparent and no other waters were impacted. The operator was contacted and instructed to place booms for containment and monitor through the weekend, followed by a run of agitating the stream bottom to push any product caught in the substrate to collect it in the next week. They also dug up the impacted soil next to the stream with shovels and removed it. Bill Otto of MSL sent photos to show that booms were placed and digging done as of late Friday, May 1. Further followup will be done as possible.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/24/2025 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Center Township, Indiana county. 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 4/24/2025
Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8231115
Permit API: 063-32778
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Center Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/24/2025
Comments: The Department received a complaint on 4/16/2025 that Diversified used farm fields to plug an abandoned well, and they did not sufficiently remediate the area. The complaint is associated with Diversified Production, LLC's Margaret E Beck 2 well site (063-32778). This well was drilled in June 2001. The well was plugged in April 2025 by NextLvL. Brian Shank (WQSS) and I completed a Complaint Inspection on 4/24/2025. The lower half of the access road was exposed soil, and upper half of the access road was seeded and mulched. The exposed, steep portion of the access road was not stabilized. There were deep ruts on the exposed, steep portion of the access road and in the seeded/mulched area of the access road. These ruts create channels down the slope of the access road and the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation (E and S). Violations will be cited for failure to implement E and S BMPs. There appeared to be a release from the pit during plugging. There was evidence of material flowing over the silt sock into the neighboring pasture, and the cows licking the area due to the salt content.

Permit API: 039-24918
Unconventional: No
County: Crawford
Municipality: Richmond Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-03-13
Comments: Onsite for a routine inspection on 3/12/2020 at 14:03pm. A 100bbl steel tank, 50bbl poly tank, and a separator are located inside an earthen dike. The annulus is not visible to inspect. A well tag is present and the well appears to be producing. The wellhead is located in a low depression with surface water surrounding the well. The 100bbl steel tank is not connected and appears to not be in use. The heat tube on the tank was observed leaking fluid. Dave Hazelet from Diversified Gas and Oil was contacted. The status of the tank was discussed and Dave indicated that a water truck will be scheduled for first thing in the morning to empty the tank. 3/13/2020 Received a phone call from Dave Hazelet at 10:42am. Dave reported that the tank is now empty and that the heat tube was plugged. Arrangements will also be made to remove the tank from the site. I conducted a follow-up visit to the site at 14:10pm and found that the tank is empty and the heat tube is plugged. The issue has been resolved.

Comments: On 2/5/20 at 1130 hrs. I conducted several inspections of Diversified Productions, LLC wells in Center Twp., Indiana Co. in response to a complaint received by the Department on 1/23/20. This included an inspection of the W B George 4 well (063-33214). Of particular concern is the destabilization of the access roads leading to these well sites and maintenance of existing BMPs along the access roads. The well pad is permanently stabilized; however, the access road is not stabilized, contributing to down-gradient erosion and sedimentation. Additional BMPs and maintenance of existing BMPs is needed to stabilize the access road. The well is equipped for production. A well tag with the permit number is affixed to the well head. A site ID sign is posted, but is illegible and does not reflect the current operator's name and contact information. An updated sign should be posted. Violations of 102.11(a)1, 102.4(b)1, and 102.22(a) are being cited for this inspection.

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Violation ID: 970926
Permit API: 117-22110
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Sullivan Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 10/05/2022
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) completed an administrative inspection on Seneca Resource's Peffer Strong 483 35H on 10/5/2022. The inspection was conducted to summarize analytical sample results from samples collected on 9/6/2022 at the well site.On 7/7/2022, violations of 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), CSL 402(b), and SWMA 301 were cited against API #117-22110 based on analytical sample results from a sample collected on 6/23/2022 indicating the presence of a regulated substance on the pad surface, off containment. Three areas with the presence of material or water with elevated conductivity were identified in the 6/23/2022 inspection report: pooled fluid near the entrance of the pad, pad material in front of the produced water offload area and pad material located just southeast of the gas processing unit's (GPUs) containment.On 9/6/2022, the pad surface area located just southeast of the GPUs' secondary containment was retaining fluid that was field measured at ~3.72mS/cm. Sample 0983-344 was collected from the pooled fluid. The analytical sample results for this sample are attached as a file and photo (photo #2). Just east of the GPUs' containment structure, a rock-lined channel used for the conveyance of stormwater into the site's sediment traps is located at the base of the pad's cut slope. On 9/6/2022, fluid within the channel was field measured at ~2.30mS/cm and sample 0983-343 was collected for the channel. The analytical sample results for this sample are attached as a file and photo (photo #3).On 9/6/2022, the secondary containment structure surrounding the wellheads and processing equipment near the center of the pad was observed to be actively overflowing. A violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.64a(e) regarding the failure to remove stormwater as soon as possible and prior to the capacity of secondary containment being reduced by 10% or more was cited against API #117-22110. Seneca Resource's notice of violation response is attached as a file and will be uploaded to eFACTS. Sample 0983-345 was collected from fluid with a sheen observed overtopping the containment structure. The analytical sample results for this sample are attached as a file and photo (photo #1).The DEP highly recommends conducting additional screening and potential remedial work.Violations of the following cited against API #117-22110 will remain outstanding at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)25 Pa. Code 78a.64a(e)

The impacted area appeared to be 40’ in length and approximately 15’ wide with a maximum depth of approximately 12 inches. No discharge was observed off the well pad and the spill did not appear to impact waters of the commonwealth. Violations are being issued for failure to control a regulated fluid resulting a release to the ground.

Permit API: 125-29197
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 1/29/2026
Comments: On January 29, 2026, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection at Range Resources Shearer Robert tank pad located in Robinson Township, Washington County following a spill that was reported to the DEP on 1/27/2026. Accompanying during today's inspection was Range Resources representative Nate Smiell.Documented in IR 4131333, according to the spill report and the phone conversation with Mr. Zofchak, at approximately 2:55 AM on January 27, 2026 a water truck was staged on the tank pad when a closed valve on the back of the truck began leaking into a bleeder valve hose, subsequently releasing Produced Water onto the gravel pad in an approximately 20 ft by 100 ft area. Water truck drivers contained the release to the graveledwell pad and began vacuuming up the pooled fluid, SPSI arrived on site on 1/27/2026 and began scraping the gravel tank pad. The release was estimated to be approximately 193 gallons, and no waters of the Commonwealth were reportedly impacted.At the time of this inspection, an Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it and in the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan, and a Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Smiell showed the Department the approximate location of the incident area and stated that SPSI finished scraping the tank pad and filled 2 roll off dumpsters with contaminated gravel on 1/27/2026. The area which appeared to be approximately 100 ft by 20 ft was observed to be recently scraped. Some spray paint was observed on the gravel to mark the areas where Mr. Smiell reported that samples were collected on 1/28/2026 in accordance with Act 2 requirements. Soil conductivity readings could not be collected due to the ground being frozen, however, the Department did not observe any visible evidence of Produced Water remaining on the graveled tank pad. Range is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, and plan for remediation of the violations. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled.Range will need to follow the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Range will also need to assess the impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the release.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the 193 gallon release of Produced Water onto the graveled tank pad.

Inspection Date: 4/17/2026
Comments: On April 17, 2026, the DEP conducted a FUI of Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc's Armstrong 2 gas well following IR4155454 where violations were continued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road. Present during today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.A NOV response has yet to be received from the operator of this gas well following IR3891447 when viols were issued however, the DEP has been in communication with the other operator who utilizes the shared portion of the access road. IR4155472 documents the other operator stating they would visit the site to assess the shared road. Observations collected of the shared access road during IR 4155454 include deep erosion rills with water actively flowing down the access road and an exposed and cracked open culvert pipe. During IR 4155454, the DEP requested the operator(s) provide the DEP with a written timeline of remedial actions to repair the access road. To date, this written timeline this has yet to be received. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the shared portion of the access road (Wildcat Road) to be graded with all erosion rills and the exposed culvert pipe removed. Dirt that appeared to be removed from the road during grading was observed to be piled up along the right side of the shared access road. Clumps of this dirt was also observed in the floodway/streambank of a stream located directly downslope and to the right of the shared access road. The broken culvert pipe was observed to be lying on the ground adjacent to the access road, another piece of culvert piping that the broken piece was connected to was still observed to be in the ground and partially buried. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/15/2026
Violation Code: 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
Violation ID: 8278412
Permit API: 123-45905
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Brokenstraw Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/15/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Conklin Lease tank battery. Mature trees at the southwest corner of the secondary containment area are either heavily stressed or dead. A brine tank is buried within the secondary containment area. PVC lines connect the drain valves of the stock tanks in containment to cutout holes in the surface of the brine tank. Evidence of previous fluid releases in the containment area are visible via crude oil staining and sawdust sprinkled over the oil-stained areas. It appears that the PVC lines connected to the two stock tanks in the southernmost end of the containment area have been the most heavily used. At the time of this inspection, the PVC lines are placed inside the cutout holes of the brine tank. However, oil-staining, visible wetness, and sawdust sprinkled around these cutout holes indicate that at one time fluid was allowed to run over the surface of the brine tank and onto the ground within the secondary containment area. Elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 3,000 uS/cm was observed beneath both of the aforementioned PVC lines.A pool of fluid was present in the southernmost end of the containment area, in what appeared to be a sump. At the time of this inspection, the fluid was observed to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 4,000 uS/cm. Soils at the bottom of the sump also had elevated specific conductance which measured in excess of 11,000 uS/cm. The floor of the secondary containment area above the sump was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 uS/cm. A drainage swale is located approximately 30 feet west of the secondary containment area wall. Upslope soil conductivity readings in the swale were observed at 96 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance in excess of 4,000 uS/cm was observed in soils within the swale directly across from the tank battery. Crude oil staining was also observed in the swale near the tank battery. The swale transitions to an UNT to Irvine Run with defined bed and banks downslope of the tank battery. The water flowing in the UNT was found to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 13,000 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance of water was observed throughout the stream at the time of this inspection. The specific conductance of water in the stream was observed to drop below 1,000 uS/cm after two confluences with apparently unaffected sources of fresh water at a point approximately 200 feet north of a culvert and the lease road which crosses the UNT. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Conklin lease.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-01-30 to Pa Gen Energy Co Llc in Wharton Twp, Potter county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Pa Gen Energy Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-01-30
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 840720
Permit API: 105-21651
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Wharton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-01-30
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of PGE's Pine Hill 1941 Well Pad in Wharton Twp, Potter County on 1/30/2019 at 1215 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a spill reported to the DEP Report hotline by Nathan Harris (PGE). It was reported that at approximately 0900 a vac truck that was moving produced water from a production tank had "collapsed". The tank was estimated to have had 25 barrels of liquid inside when it collapsed. DEP WQS, Jonathan Pennings and I arrived onsite at 1215 hours. When we arrived the truck was still in place and crew was observed sucking up fluids from the pad surface. We observed the vac truck(see photo #1) and the impacted area (photo #2 & 14). Puddles and slush mixes were field measured with a PCSTestr returning readings ranging from ~2.0 ms/cm to ~15.0 ms/cm (see photos #3, 4 & 5). We spoke with Erick Duzick (PGE Completions Engineer) onsite who explained the vac trucks relief valve was frozen solid which had caused the truck to create a vacuum which in return caused the vac truck tank to implode. The truck driver reported that liquid was released from the back hatch and from a small hole in the side of the tank (see photos #10 &11). It appeared that most of the liquid would have released from the back hatch. The truck driver also mentioned that by the time he got a ride and another vac truck onsite, approximately 1.5 hours had passed before clean-up was underway. He also estimated (using the site glass) that ~25 barrels were in the truck before it imploded. The other vac truck driver that was onsite for clean-up explained to us that when he dropped off the recovered liquids at Clermont Storage Facility that he could let us know how much was recovered from the pad surface. Crew began scraping pad material when we were onsite. See photos #8, 9, & 12 showing the excavator and pile of impacted pad material/snow recovered. The material was then temporarily transferred to a sheet of plastic until a roll-off truck could make it onsite. A wrecker was also on the way to transport the vac truck. Observations made in the field confirmed that the release was more than 42 gallons. The operator should refer to the procedures outlined in 25 Pa Code Section 78a66(c)(2) pertaining to remediating releases greater than 42 gallons. Sample 0935-404 was collected by Jonathan approximately 10 feet north of the containment surrounding the production tanks. This sample was a snow mix from the pile of excavated material and will be submitted for metals only. We departed the site at 1330 hours. Due to observations made during the course of the inspection violations of the following are cited against Well Permit API #105-21651: 35 P.S. Section 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code Section 78a.57(a) 35 P.S. Section 6018.301 Operator called on 1/31/2019 and reported that the clean-up was completed and screening of the impacted area was completed. Violations will remain open until remediation and reporting is conducted in compliance with 25 Pa. Code Section 78a.66.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/23/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8235146
Permit API: 015-23438
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/27/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Broadleaf Holdings" Marcellus well site. Tory Rogers called the DEP on Friday morning May 23, 2025 to report a release of approximately 9 gallons of diesel based drilling mud released from a flare stack to the pad surface that morning. I met with Tory Rogers, Jim Brown, Megan DePue (all 3 Repsol), and Scotty Brown (DEP, OGI) on site. While drilling a future Marcellus Shale well there was a control issue, so they lit the flare stack to burn off natural gas incurred. Some drilling mud blew out of the flare stack, estimated at 7 gallons onto pad containment, and 9 gallons on the pad surface. Rogers showed us where the flare stack released drilling mud. Resource Environmental directed excavation to remove pad material the drilling mud impacted, which was approximately a 10'X60' area. They completed the cleanup around 1600 hrs the same day the release occurred. The material is in 2 dumpsters on the NE corner of the pad. I got a 1.5 ppm reading with a 10.6 eV MiniRae photoionization detector (PID) from the removed pad material, and a 0.0 ppm PID reading from the remediated pad surface, which indicates the cleanup sufficiently removed the impacted pad material. Drill cuttings in a dumpster near the drill rig gave a 135.7 ppm reading. Violations cited to the 015-23893 drilling permit are considered immediately corrected.Rogers explained they increased the density of the drill mud from 12.8 lbs/gal to 13.5 lbs/gal to provide more well control.Repsol laid the containment on this pad on February 26 thru March 3, 2025. Felt liner (130 mil thickness) went down first, then wood/steel mats. Fine gravel is used to fill gaps between the mats.Precision Drilling 110 started drilling 4 new Marcellus wells at this site on April 1 2025, and expect to finish drilling around June 10, 2025. There are also 4 existing Marcellus wells here. They drill on water based mud for the vertical section, then switch to diesel based mud for the kickoff (curve) and horizontal section.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity (EC) of 0.68-1.7 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.62FJLP

Comments: On 12/12/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the GH5 well site following an incident report submitted to the Department on 12/11/2023 (376984). I was accompanied by Andrew Perine of CNX. Additional representatives from CNX, Pine Belt Energy Services, and Penn E and R onsite.I contacted the operator on 12/11/2023 to follow up on the incident. The material involved was brine water. There is a pipeline off of CNX's GH 5 well site; the drip leg for the site was next to the pipeline and they believe that is the source of the spill. The leak is on the pad and goes downhill approximately 100 feet and is approximately 20 feet in width. The spill did not make it to the stream below. The stream downslope of the spill area is Lightner Run along Lightner Run Road. The operator was waiting for dumpsters to arrive on site at the time. They had the spill isolated and the clean-up crew from Pine Belt Energy Services is on-site. They roughly estimated the spill to be 84 gallons, however at that moment, they are unsure of the extent of the spill depth-wise. The operator is going to follow Act 2 guidelines and have their third-party crew analyze the site. The following was observed during inspection on 12/12/2023:Excavation of impacted material was occurring and waste placed into lined dumpsters. At the time, two barrels were estimated to have been excavated. The labels not updated to site - I recommend that the labels are updated (Photos 1, 2).Silt fence added below impacted area. I recommend that routine maintenance is performed on fence to ensure proper placement. Some parts of fence slumping (Photo 3).The impacted area was outline with orange paint (Photos 4-6). The area was approximately 80 feet in length and 12 feet in width further down slope (Photo 6). Closer to the well, another area was marked in orange and was approximately 20 feet in length (Photos 14-16, 25).Conductivity readings were taken within the impacted area. The noted readings ranged from 0.09 m/S - 19.29 m/S (specific locations noted in photo captions). Higher reading moving up the slope and in the area of origin near the well site (Photos 7-24). They estimated that the impacted material towards the bottom of the slope was around two inches in depth and deeper towards the top of the slope. Two feet were dug to reach the impacted material. There is a stream called Lightner Run that is on the opposite side of Lightner Run Road, below the impacted area. The road is approximately 335 feet southwest (below) of the silt fence and the stream is approximately 430 feet southwest (below) of the silt fence. Penn E and R is going to take samples within the stream.Due to the release of production fluid over a barrel, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/28/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of a petroleum based fluid. The release was found by Zac Subra around 12:30 pm on Monday, 10/28/24. Over the preceding weekend, containment was being pulled and placed into dumpsters for disposal.The impacted area was estimated to be about 50' by 100' although the surface staining was not continuous throughout the entire area. The impacts were just to the southwest of the wells. The actual size of the release will be better known as the impacted area is excavated.Around the time the release was discovered, it was noted that one of the dumpsters holding containment was leaking some sort of fluid. The dumpster was placed on secondary containment to further evaluate its contents and ensure that it is suitable to travel on the road. The leaking dumpster created a second impacted area that was approximately 25' by 15'. This second location was near the edge of the pad roughly south of the original impacted area.At the time of inspection, there was no evidence of impacts beyond the pad surface. Tobias was expected to begin excavating the impacted area before the end of the day. Penn E and R was also scheduled to begin sampling for remediation under Act 2.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a).
